html:
A Turkish chief in northwestern Anatolia who founded the Ottoman state around 1300. The dynasty and the Ottoman Empire are named after him: Ottoman comes from Osman.

He ruled a small principality around Söğüt in Bithynia, on the frontier with the Byzantine Empire. After the Mongols broke the power of the Seljuk sultans of Anatolia in 1243, the region split into many small Turkish states, called beyliks. Osman's was one of the smallest, but it lay next to rich Byzantine towns.

His warriors raided and took Byzantine land, and in 1302 he beat a Byzantine army at the Battle of Bapheus, which drew more fighters to his side. Very little about him is documented; much comes from legends written down later, such as his dream of a tree growing from his body to shade the world. Around the time of his death, his son Orhan took the city of Bursa, which became the first Ottoman capital. A century and a half later his descendant Mehmed II took Constantinople.
sum: A Turkish chief in northwestern Anatolia who founded the Ottoman state around 1300. The dynasty and the Ottoman Empire are named after him: Ottoman comes from Osman.
